newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss DIAX enters alliance with SBC of U.S..
newsitem.headline: Swiss DIAX enters alliance with SBC of U.S..

text.p: DIAX, the joint telecom company formed by Swiss utilities, said it had picked SBC Communications Inc. of the U.S. as an alliance partner to enter the Swiss telecommunications market as of 1998.

DIAX was formed earlier this year by six Swiss utilities, which plan to use their communications infrastructure to offer telecommunications services for private and business customers in Switzerland once the telecommunications monopoly disappears.
SBC will provide DIAX with the expertise to operate in a deregulated environment, DIAX said in a statement.
DIAX said its entry into the market depends on developments in the regulatory framework and particularly the allocation of mobile telephony frequencies.
"The combination of both wirebased and mobile services will allow the creation of a fully capable Swiss competitor in the liberalised telecommunications market," DIAX said.

The utilities in DIAX are Aare-Tessin Electricity AG (Atel), BKW FMB Energy AG (BKW), Centralschweizerische Kraftwerke AG (CKW), Elektrizitaetsgesellschaft Laufenberg AG (EGL), L'Energie de l'Ouest-Suisse (EOS) and Northostschweizerische Kraftwerke (NOK).

DIAX will not only be competing with a partially-privatised Swiss Telecom, but also a consortium recently formed by Swiss Federal Railways SBB, the Migro cooperative and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) ) with the name of Newtelco AG.
The six utilities have been preparing to enter the Swiss telecommunications market for around a year.
The services DIAX plans to offer include basic voice services, including ISDN and Internet connections, data transfer and computer networks and mobile telephone services.

On April 1 SBC Communications and Pacific Telesis Group announced they intended to merge in early 1997 to create a company with annual revenue over $21 billion, one of the largest telecommuncations groups in the U.S.
